tagline: Builds a website by typing into a Notion-style document that compiles to a static site.
verdictSummary: Typedream's idea is that editing a website should feel like editing a document: slash commands, blocks, no layout panel. Building that editing surface properly — block model, drag handles, keyboard behaviour, undo that does the right thing — is the multi-day part, and it is the whole product. The static-site compilation underneath is straightforward. You can get there, but you are writing an editor, not a site generator.
coreLoopDIY: Write a page as a block document with slash commands, pick from a small set of section blocks rather than positioning anything, and compile the result to a static site you deploy yourself.
whatYouLose: hosted publishing with a domain attached in one click
the template gallery and its designed starting points
form submissions collected without a backend of your own
the CMS layer for a blog or a collection of items
whyPeopleStillPay: Because publishing is the feature. Typing a page is pleasant everywhere; having it live at your own domain thirty seconds later, with SSL handled, is what people are actually buying.
notes: Framed around the document-style editing surface rather than the site output, since that surface is both the product's identity and where the build time actually goes.
prompt:
Build a website editor where the editing surface is a block document, not a canvas.

Editor: a block-based document editor. Enter creates a new block; a slash command opens a block picker; blocks can be dragged to reorder by a handle; backspace at the start of an empty block merges upward. Undo and redo operate on block-level operations, not on raw text. Get these behaviours right before adding any block types — they are what makes the surface feel like a document rather than a form.

Block types, and no more: heading, paragraph, image, button, columns (two or three), card grid, FAQ accordion, pricing table, logo strip, form, and divider. Each block exposes a handful of options through a small popover, never a properties panel with arbitrary CSS. Positioning is not a control the user has; layout comes from the block and the theme.

Theme: a token file defining a type scale, a colour palette, spacing and radius. Blocks consume tokens only. Changing the palette restyles the whole site, which is the point of a constrained system.

Preview: desktop, tablet and mobile widths, with an overflow check that flags any block whose content breaks its container at the narrow width — the failure users only discover after publishing.

Compilation: emit a static site — semantic HTML, one CSS file built from the tokens, images resized to responsive sets at build time, and no client-side JavaScript except for the accordion and the mobile menu. The output must score well on Lighthouse without further work, because a page builder that emits a heavy page has failed at its one job.

Forms: a form block emits a plain HTML form posting to a URL the user configures. Do not build a submission backend; document how to point it at a form service or a small endpoint of their own.

Storage: the document as JSON on disk, so a site can live in a git repository and be diffed.

Deployment: emit a folder of static files and document deploying it to one target end to end, including attaching a custom domain.

Out of scope: hosted publishing, a template marketplace, a CMS or collections, memberships, and ecommerce.

faq.q: Can I export my Typedream site?
faq.a: Not usefully. Typedream publishes to its own hosting and does not export the source, so migrating means rebuilding the page here. Since the block model is similar, the copy transfers by paste and the layout takes an hour.

faq.q: Why constrain the blocks so tightly?
faq.a: Because the alternative is a canvas editor, which is a fundamentally larger build and produces worse sites in non-designers' hands. The constraint is what lets a token change restyle everything and what keeps the emitted HTML clean.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: The editor runs locally for nothing. Publishing is static files, which any of the free static hosts serve at no cost, so the only real expense is the domain — roughly ten to fifteen dollars a year against Typedream's monthly plan.

faq.q: What is the one thing that does not survive the rebuild?
faq.a: One-click publish. Typedream takes you from typing to a live page on your own domain without leaving the app. Here, publishing is a build step, a deploy command and a DNS record, which is fine once and tiresome every time you fix a typo.
